commitResults.messageTitle: Add date bounds to recurring commitments
commitResults.messageBody:
Recurring commitments currently block their weekday indefinitely, so semester events reserve study time after they end.

Store optional inclusive date bounds, apply them to overlap and scheduling, and persist them in a backward-compatible version 3 format. Extend commands, rendering, documentation, and regression coverage so bounded series survive restart without changing legacy behaviour.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/scheduleflow/cli/CommandParser.java
#	test/ui-test-plan.md

Students with project meetings and other fixed events can only enter
weekly commitments, so a single event either blocks every week or is
not recorded and the planner may schedule study time over it.

Add `commitment add n/NAME on/YYYY-MM-DD start/HHmm d/MINUTES`. A
one-time commitment is represented as a commitment whose inclusive
start and end dates are equal, exposed by Commitment.isOneTime(). This
reuses the issue #64 date-range model: occursOn already blocks only
that date in planning and schedule views, overlaps already compares
the actual occurrence with recurring series (including skipped dates)
and other one-time commitments, and version 3/4 storage already
persists the dates, so no record component, command type or storage
version is needed and existing saved data loads unchanged.

The parser maps on/ to the derived weekday and equal dates for add and
edit, rejecting on/ combined with day/ or from/until. The service
rejects skipping a one-time commitment, rejects day/ alone on one
(its weekday follows its date), and drops weekly skips when an edit
produces a one-time result; the constructor rejects a one-time record
whose only date is skipped. Confirmations show "One-time on DATE
(Weekday)", and commitment list adds a separate one-time section
ordered by date after the weekly groups.

A weekly series entered with identical from/ and until/ dates has one
occurrence and is now displayed as one-time; UI-017's expectation for
that input is updated. Help, usage hints, User Guide, Developer Guide
and the UI plan are updated, and UI-018 covers the packaged flow.

Checks: 279 JUnit tests and Checkstyle (gradlew build), 12 UI-runner
tests, 18/18 packaged UI scenarios, and release tests (18/18 with -ea
plus distribution launch) passed on Java 25.0.4.

Depends on #79 (skipping occurrences), which builds on #78.

per date, checks each against stored commitments with the existing
rejectOverlaps in date order, and appends all of them in one candidate.
Continuous mode splits at midnight and omits an end date reached exactly
at midnight; date stepping never passes the last generated date.

Reusing the one-time model keeps planning, storage, listing and deletion
unchanged, and building one local candidate makes each request atomic:
a rejection leaves the source snapshot and ID counter untouched.
